_meta.source: book/on_the_origin_of_risk (Timlett 2025), ch. 5 (Café state, PicBreeder, squash court)

failure_modes: Mistaking a hub for a hedge and never moving from it
Judging an intermediate state by its own payoff and discarding it
Holding a hub in an environment too stable to repay the lower payoff
gloss: Occupy a state from which many valuable states are cheap to reach
invariants: A hub's value lies in the transitions it makes cheap, not in its own payoff
The value is realised only by moving after new information arrives
mechanism: Some states are worth occupying not for their own payoff but because they lower the cost of moving to many other valuable states. A café between home and park, the centre of a squash court, and PicBreeder parent images that breed into skulls and cars all work this way. A hub raises the {{information_dividend}} by cutting transition costs. It differs from a hedge: a hedge is a static allocation across positions, while a hub pays only when the occupant actually moves in response to information.
